claims.object_text: benign familial neonatal seizures (BFNS) and developmental epileptic encephalopathy (DEE)
claims.quote: Autosomal dominant mutations of the KCNQ2 gene can cause two epileptic disorders: benign familial neonatal seizures (BFNS) and developmental epileptic encephalopathy (DEE).

claims.object_text: 95% of BFNS patients became seizure free, whereas the seizures stopped only in 73% of those with DEE
claims.quote: After treatment began, 95% of BFNS patients became seizure free, whereas the seizures stopped only in 73% of those with DEE.

claims.object_text: Phenobarbital and sodium channel blockers were the most used treatment in BFNS
claims.quote: Phenobarbital and sodium channel blockers were the most used treatment in BFNS.

claims.object_text: Most of the DEE patients (95%) needed polytherapy for seizure control and even that did not prevent subsequent developmental impairment (77%)

Missense mutations were discovered in 96% of DEE patients;

claims.object_text: Phenobarbital or carbamazepine appears to be the most effective antiseizure medication for children with a "benign" variant
